title: Desktop application, view model and widgets
objective: Finish the desktop's one-path work and make its structure match its documented layers: the defects fixed, the crop fully on the one draft driver with a declared angle stepper and a proxy stage, one start refusal, draft rounds that cost no extra frame, state owned by the seam that uses it, evidence that drives the shipped paths and the live-agent path, layers the repository check can enforce, and tests that prove each behaviour once.
context_summary: The consolidation gave the desktop one pure draft state machine behind one gesture slot and refusal function, one owner call helper, one frame presenter, an idle loop that is asleep and a descriptor-driven control path with no module names in production UI code. It left the crop with its own lifecycle, refusal, notice and angle control beside the one driver, evidence-only slider messages, draft.begin/cancel/reapply as runtime hops, a 117-field Editor whose seams are files rather than owners, an unmeasured per-region derivation framework, layering leaks the boundary check cannot see, and about 950 lines of mock panels in the widget crate. Decisions: docs/decisions.md "Post-consolidation review"; constraints: docs/design/post-consolidation.md; the desktop design: docs/design/develop-workspace.md. Every Iced runtime hop costs about one displayed frame on the M4 (performance rule 12), which is why gesture owner calls stay synchronous.

tasks.description: Make a double-click on the crop angle's rail reset the angle to 0 and send the change, instead of only rewriting the text box.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix.

`view/tools_panel.rs`'s `angle_stepper` wires the rail's reset to `Message::Crop(CropMessage::AngleText("0".into()))`, and `app/crop.rs`'s `CropMessage::AngleText` handler only assigns `self.crop_angle = text`; the draft, the rail and the canvas keep the pressed angle after the reset runs.

Every generic slider's double-click reset (`ResetField`) sets the field's default value and sends it as a real change; the crop angle is the one stepper that does not, because it predates the generic control path. No test or capture covers a double-click on the crop rail today.

The fix here is behavioural only: send the same change `NudgeAngle` sends. Removing the angle's separate model and messages once it is declared as a generic stepper is separate, later work in this plan.

tasks.description: Report a truncated diagnostics log: count events dropped past the cap, write one truncation record at finish, and fail an evidence run whose log was truncated.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix.

`diagnostics.rs`'s background writer keeps `Record::Event(value) if count < 4096 && !failed`; every event past the cap falls into the catch-all arm and is dropped with no record at all. `finish()` already returns `false` on a write or flush failure, but a truncated run still returns `true`.

A drag logs 4-5 diagnostic events per input; a recorded burst run reached 1,756 events for 360 inputs, so a `--data-root` session stops logging after roughly 850 drag inputs. An evidence run near the cap would silently lose the `round_trip_ms` records `editor-latency` reads, with nothing saying so.
Keep the cap; only make the drop loud. `finish()` failing on truncation is what lets evidence treat it exactly like the write failure it already handles.

tasks.description: Refuse Undo, Redo and Restore while a draft is open, through the one refusal rule, with the reason in the status bar.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix.

Owner decision (2026-09-26): Undo, Redo and Restore are refused while a draft is open, with the reason in the status bar, matching every other discrete commit (`app/actions.rs`'s `gesture_refusal` check before a mask command or a preset apply).

Today Cmd+Z is always mapped in `app/keymap.rs`; `app/sync.rs`'s `command()`, which every discrete commit calls, refuses only on `self.busy`; and `state/title.rs`'s `derive()` computes `can_undo`/`can_redo` from `editable` (state open, `can_edit()`, not busy) with no draft check, so the title bar shows Undo and Redo enabled during a draft.

Committing Undo, Redo or Restore over an open draft marks this client's own draft conflicted today, and `state/canvas.rs` reports it with one of three near-identical sentences ("Another client committed revision N while your slider draft was open", naming a mask gesture or a crop draft the same way) that is untrue: no other client committed anything. The user guide documents this as intended today ("another client, or your own Undo, Redo or Restore" marks the draft "Changed elsewhere"), so it needs updating along with the design.

Refuse at the UI entry points that call `command()` for Undo, Redo and Restore, not inside `command()` itself, since evidence's `api` step also goes through `command()` and must keep being able to exercise them directly for other checks.

tasks.description: Drive sliders in evidence and tests through the widgets' own messages and delete the evidence-only slider messages and the dead cancel message.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation.

`ControlMessage::SliderMoved` and `SliderReleased` (`app/message.rs`, handled in `app/controls.rs`) are sent only by the evidence driver (`app/evidence.rs`) and by tests; the slider widget itself sends `Fraction` and `Released`, wired in `view/tools_panel.rs`. `CancelEdit` is sent by no widget at all, only by one test.

The two paths disagree: `SliderMoved` on a non-drafting slider goes straight to `slider_moved(...)` and skips the `editable()` check `control_value` makes for `Fraction`; `SliderReleased` calls `release()` on whatever gesture is open, while `Released` only releases a control that is drafting. So the `slider` evidence step and the slider tests prove a path the shipped widget never takes.

Convert the evidence `slider` step to send `Fraction`/`Released`, computed from each scripted value through the same `NumberSpec` the widget uses, so evidence values round-trip through a fraction and back exactly; give tests a `slide()` helper over the same messages.

Delete `SliderMoved`, `SliderReleased`, `Editor::slider_moved` and `CancelEdit` once nothing sends them; add a `check-repository` rule (or a test) that refuses a control message that only evidence or a test constructs, so a future evidence-only message is caught the same way.

tasks.description: Put the crop fully on the one draft driver: the shared commit, cancel and reapply messages, one refusal behind Apply, one conflict notice, a frame opened from the recipe rows with no change queue, and the crop's values and geometry taken from the core.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation.

Crop already runs on the core `draft.*` lifecycle, but keeps its own `CropMessage::{Apply, Cancel, Reapply}` beside the shared `DraftMessage::{Commit, Cancel, Reapply}`, which `app/gesture.rs`'s `release_refusal` already routes crop through via `crop_refusal`. It also keeps its own keymap branch in `app/keymap.rs`, two extra `NoticeAction` variants and a `mask: bool` flag on the draft bar, and three near-identical "Changed elsewhere" notices in `state/canvas.rs` that differ only by naming a slider draft, a mask gesture or a crop draft.

Whether Apply can run is decided three times with three different wordings: `state/tools.rs`'s `can_apply` (`enabled && !gesture_conflicted`, no wording), `state/canvas.rs`'s `apply_reason` (conflicted, preview or busy, one set of sentences) and `app/crop.rs`'s `crop_refusal` (busy, preview, conflicted, plus the output error, a different set). The two view-model copies leave out the output check the app itself makes, so the button can read enabled while the app would refuse the request.

The start waits for a truncated, full-resolution render to learn a size every `recipe.describe` row already reports as `input_stage`; that produces a pending state, `app/crop.rs`'s 32-deep `QUEUED_CHANGES` with rail coalescing, "prospective" angle text duplicated in `app/crop.rs` and `state/tools.rs`, and currency checks. Open the frame synchronously instead, from an existing crop's row (`input_stage` and `values`) or, for a new crop, the row at the insertion index; add an `output_stage` to `RecipeDescription` for the append case, since it does not exist there today.

The start also re-derives geometry the core already reports: `app/crop.rs`'s `orientation_ahead` parses `ORIENTATION_EFFECT` payloads and folds them on the desktop, although the develop-workspace design states "the desktop folds no geometry itself"; `crop_draft.rs` re-implements the core's own `refit` inline in `rebase` instead of calling it; and the crop aspect vocabulary is spelled twice (`crop/module.rs`'s presets and `crop_draft.rs`'s `parse_ratio`), where "free" means a different thing in each. Read committed values and the orientation ahead of a row from `recipe.describe` instead of parsing payloads.

Owner decision (2026-09-26): a crop draft opens before the stage's pixels arrive, so the section is live at once and the canvas shows the frame once the stage renders — delivered here; showing the input stage itself from a proxy at Fit is separate, later work in this plan. The owner also decided that `CropMessage::Cancel` on a draft that is still starting now cancels it outright rather than being silently ignored as it is today; record that as the intended behaviour in the develop-workspace design, since it is more honest than doing nothing.

tasks.description: Run `draft.begin`, `draft.cancel` and `draft.reapply` synchronously on the desktop thread, like `draft.set`, keeping only `draft.commit` as an owner task.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed.
Owner decision (2026-09-26): `draft.begin`, `draft.cancel` and `draft.reapply` run synchronously on the desktop thread like `draft.set`, proven by a press-to-first-frame measurement.

`draft.set` is already synchronous because every runtime hop costs about one displayed frame on the M4 at 120 Hz (performance rule 12, measured). `draft_begin_task` and the cancel and reapply tasks (`app/tasks.rs`) are still owner tasks, although the core implements all three as session-only operations behind `crates/luxforge-core/src/api/methods.rs`'s `draft.begin`/`draft.cancel`/`draft.reapply` handlers, none of which writes the catalog. So the first move of every slider, mask and crop gesture waits one avoidable hop for `Begun` before any `draft.set` can go.

The asynchrony is also why most of the driver's race handling exists: `app/draft.rs`'s `Round` enum tracks Begin, Reapply and Cancel rounds that would not exist if those calls were synchronous; `Gesture::Closing` (`app/gesture.rs`) and its "still opening"/"still closing" refusals exist only to block a new gesture while an old begin or cancel is in flight; and four of the seven draft races the mask work found (Apply before begin answers, a late begin adopted by a newer gesture, a late failed reapply, Discard adopting a session that still holds the draft) become impossible by construction once nothing is left in flight to race.

`CoreDraft` keeps only the `Set` and `Commit` rounds after this change; `Round::{Begin,Reapply,Cancel}`, `Gesture::Closing` and the three task wrappers and their message variants (`DraftMessage::{Begun,Reapplied,Cancelled}`) are deleted along with the race tests that exist only to prove states that no longer occur; name each deleted race test with why its race is now structurally impossible.

The develop-workspace design's message-flow section documents today's asynchronous shape ("the other four are owner tasks whose answers come back as one `Message::Draft` family"); it needs updating to describe the synchronous begin, cancel and reapply, leaving only commit as an owner task.

tasks.description: Hold an armed brush as view state and open its core draft at the press, so no empty draft exists between strokes.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed.

After each stroke commits, the desktop opens an empty `mask.add-stroke` draft immediately so the next press can call `draft.set` at once. That empty draft needs handling everywhere: every other gesture must take it over (`app/gesture.rs`'s `claim_slot`), every mask command must put it down first (`disarm`), release must refuse it, and a commit made elsewhere while it is open rebases it silently (`rebase_armed_brush`) instead of raising the usual conflict notice. tasks.description: Render the live-agent path in evidence: a scripted step that edits through a second client, with the event sync on in evidence runs, and move the "Changed elsewhere" frames onto it.
extra_context: Wave 5, tests.

Live agents editing alongside a person are a headline capability, and their changes reach the screen through one path: the owner wakes the desktop, a sync message fires, `events.since` answers, a refresh for another client's change runs, and the draft is marked conflicted. Evidence runs switch that path off (`app/mod.rs` gates the events subscription on no evidence being active, and `app/sync.rs`'s sync-when-wanted check returns early during an evidence run), so no rendered run shows another client's change arriving; it is covered only by unit tests in `app/tasks.rs` and the sync tests.

Today the `basic` and `workspace` smokes' "Changed elsewhere" frames come from the desktop's own client committing through the evidence driver's `api_step`, and the captured notice text says "Another client committed revision N", which is not what happened.

Add an `agent` evidence step (in `luxforge-evidence`) that sends through a second client registered on the same owner; enable the event subscription in evidence runs; settle the step on the sync's refresh reaching the screen. Move the conflict frames of the `basic` and `workspace` smokes onto this step.
Events that name their subject, a shape landing in the core service work, is what the sync's refresh reads; this task's `agent` step depends on that shape being in place first.

tasks.description: Key the photo surface's GPU slots by a surface id carried in its primitive, so two surfaces can be on screen at once.
extra_context: Wave 6, roadmap groundwork.

Blocked: starts with the library milestone on the roadmap, whose virtualized browsing across many photos (a grid, filmstrip or side-by-side compare) is the first place a second photo surface would appear on screen at once.

Iced keeps one rendering pipeline per primitive type, and `luxforge-ui/src/photo_surface.rs` holds one set of GPU tiles per layer for the whole application. Two photo surfaces drawn in the same frame today would overwrite each other's textures and uniforms, both would show whichever was prepared last, and both would re-upload every frame instead of only on a version change.

Key the pipeline's slots by a surface id carried in the primitive, and release a surface's slots by that id when it goes away. Library thumbnails do not need this: they can use Iced's own image widget with handles built outside `view()`, since the extra hop matters little for a grid of small images.
